text:
maria: Proposal: implement a "preemptible stream stabilizer" for mixed capacity pools. goal: reduce duplicate final tokens and small content gaps during node evictions.

aj: quick context — what are we observing?

maria: during ~30s eviction windows we see a 40% uptick in stream anomalies and a 25% rise in requeues. clients sometimes get a mid-stream token swap without proper KV warmup.

kai: is KV cache warming the blocker or the proxy cutover ordering?

maria: both. current drain causes proxy to open a continuation on the target before its KV prefix is ready -> chunk reordering or tiny missing tails.

ops-bot: NODE_EVICT: node/gpu-spot-198 scheduled for termination in 60s; cordon+drain started.

jen: what's the low-risk quick fix?

maria: three shortlisted options:
- lightweight handshake: origin emits a HANDOFF event to client+target; target prefetches KV prefix, replies READY, origin closes over. adds ~40-80ms to hot path but strong correctness.
- edge requeue: let origin attempt to finish for up to 10s, then requeue remaining work into stable queue with idempotency token. fewer runtime changes, higher replays.
- split policy: handshake for long streams (>3s), requeue short requests. prefer this hybrid.

sam: do all clients propagate session ids? mobile/web/SDK?

maria: most do via x-session; fallback is server-generated session token sent in a tiny handshake event.

kai: implementation surface: runtime needs prefetch endpoint and "accept-continuation" flag; proxy adds HANDOFF flow and waits for READY ack. autoscaler lifecycle hook to raise prefetch concurrency during eviction signals.

aj: impact on SLOs and cost?

maria: estimated +35ms p50 on affected streams, replay spike cut by ~80%, tail reduced ~200-400ms. cost: modest extra egress and memory for KV prefetch; rough: ~1.5 GPU-hours/day at our current eviction rate if we route bursts to ondemand. ops to refine.

jen: monitoring: record handoff_attempts, handoff_success, prefetch_latency, requeue_count, stream_replay_rate. alert if handoff_success < 99% in 15m. add Grafana panels for bucketed tail across eviction boundaries.

sam: mixed-pool routing concern: if ondemand is saturated, new short requests could 503. proposal: fallback to delayed queue with Retry-After header and increment throttle metrics.

maria: also propose a small reserved ondemand burst capacity during eviction windows to reduce user-visible failures; cost vs UX tradeoff.

aj: I'll own infra signoff and cost estimate.

ops-bot: RFC_CREATED: docs/internal/preemptible-stream-stabilizer draft at https://go/internal/preemptible-stream-stabilizer

jen: rollout plan: feature-flag the prefetch endpoint and handshake separately; canary on staging, then us-west-2 mixed-pool for 1 week, then global ramp. include SDK compatibility migration (notify sdk-team).

maria: test plan: simulate evictions in staging, fuzz missing session_id, run 1k-stream correctness test, load test ondemand burst behavior.

kai: small runtime nit: avoid handshake for streams <3s to reduce overhead.

maria: agreed; threshold configurable.

aj: added: add observability for streams that cross an eviction marker.

maria: will add metrics and a lightweight canary runbook. PR for prefetch endpoint + unit tests coming today.

ops-bot: DEPLOY: staging/preemptible-stream-stabilizer PR-78 deployed to staging at 1920033350 by maria.
